newsitem.title: USA: Western N.Y. Monday power slips on milder weather.
newsitem.headline: Western N.Y. Monday power slips on milder weather.

text.p: Day-ahead electricity prices in western New York weakened Friday on forecasts for milder temperatures in the region over the next several days.
But Monday power deliveries to New England and eastern New York remained firm on rumours of a plant problem in New York City and reduced spot supplies from Hydro-Quebec.
Temperatures are expected to moderate to near or slightly above normal Saturday and Sunday in the Northeast, and likely to continue normal or slightly above early next week.
In western NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Monday dropped to $25.00-$27.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) from Thursday's $28.00-$29.00.
Western NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Monday fell to $16.00-17.00 from $17.50-18.50 Thursday.
Spot availability in the western half of the state continued to improve with the 832 megawatt (MW) Fitzpatrick nuclear plant approaching full output after being taken off line last week.

Despite expected milder weather in the region, prices in eastern NYPP and the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL) firmed on talk of a weekend shutdown of the 825 MW Poletti station in Astoria, N.Y., and reduced spot availability from Quebec.
But New York Power Authority, which operates Poletti, said there is no mechanical problem at the plant, and has no plans to take it off line this weekend.
Sources at Hydro-Quebec said there was "minimal" reduction in spot power to NEPOOL to address reliability concerns.
Thursday, the Canadian utility cut spot supplies to the region due to strong heating demand in the province.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices for Monday delivery in the eastern half of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) firmed $32.50-$33.50 from $31.00-$32.00 Thursday.
Off-peak, non-firm power for day-ahead delivery in eastern NYPP tighted to $23.00-$24.00 from $21.00-$23.00 Thursday.
Peak, non-firm NEPOOL electricity prices at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border (including transmission costs) widened to $32.00-$35.00 from $33.00-$35.00 Thursday.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for next-day delivery at the NU border stayed near $28.00 Thursday.

The two units at the Indian Point nuclear complex north of New York City remained shut. The 975 MW unit 2, which was shut January 18 to correct problems with a feedwater valve, will likely restart next week. The 965 MW unit 3 was expected to stay idled through mid-February for replacement work in its primary containment area.
Swing natural gas values at the New York City gate slipped to the $3.45 per million British thermal units level from Thursday's $3.60-$3.80.
